title: Residency waiver handoff & risk acceptance template
content:
Purpose:
This working template is intended for cross-functional handoffs when a customer requests a temporary or permanent residency waiver (i.e., explicit exception allowing request routing or storage outside their nominated region). It codifies the minimal information Sales must collect, the risk profile summary Legal and Security need, the operator testing and telemetry required, and a clear sign-off/rollback path.

Scope and audience:
- Audience: Sales engineering, Solutions Engineering, Oncall SRE, Product privacy lead, Legal/compliance reviewer, Customer Success (CS).
- Scope: Exceptions to standard region-pinning and data locality commitments for hosted and dedicated customers. Not for Private on-prem installs (those follow contract-specific procedures).

High-level rules (do not override without exec sign-off):
1) No permanent cross-border storage of regulated PII without Legal/Privacy sign-off and updated contract addendum.
2) Waivers must have a clearly defined TTL (expiration date) and telemetry gating for re-evaluation before expiry.
3) All waivers create an auditable record: waiver request form -> risk memo -> approval signatures -> operational runbook -> telemetry dashboard.

Minimum information Sales must collect before filing waiver request:
- Customer name, tenant id, primary contact + security contact.
- Requested deviation (eg route US requests to eu-west-1 temporarily; allow cache spill to global edge).
- Business justification and timeline (start, TTL, rationale).
- Data types affected (tokens, embeddings, logs, user-uploaded files).
- Any downstream systems in other regions.
- Known regulatory constraints (GDPR, CCPA, APAC data localization laws).
- Customer attestation on data sensitivity (are they storing regulated PII?).

Risk summary template (to be completed by SE + Privacy):
- Risk category (Legal / Technical / Operational / Reputational): <one-line>
- Likelihood: low|medium|high
- Impact: low|medium|high
- Mitigations planned: short bullets (e.g. pseudonymize tokens, TTL-based cache invalidation, encryption-in-transit+at-rest).
- Evidence required before approval: list (e.g. DLP config, KMS scope, proof of region pin turned off for tenant).

Operational acceptance criteria (SRE checklist):
- Tenant routing configuration changes reviewed and staged in sandbox.
- Synthetic test suite passing: cross-region latency + correctness tests for 3 scenarios (small prompt, long prompt with cache, embeddings-heavy batch).
- Telemetry created: waiver-specific dashboard with these charts: global request distribution, percent routed outside pinned region, error rate, token volume delta, cache miss spike.
- Alerting thresholds defined and tested (eg >2% cross-region routing sustained for 15m -> page SRE).
- Rollback automation exists: single-command rollback that reinstates region pin and drains in-flight requests.

Telemetry and evidence pack (what to store in the waiver folder):
- Waiver request form (PDF/record).
- SE risk memo (signed by product privacy).
- Legal approval email/thread (PDF).
- SRE runbook (operational steps, rollback command).
- Test outputs (synthetic-run logs + hashes of test requests).
- Retention policy for telemetry and evidence (minimum 2 years or per contract).

Sign-off matrix (minimum approvers):
- Sales (requesting AE) - acknowledges business need and duration
- Solutions/SE - confirms technical scope
- Product Privacy/Legal - accepts/regulates legal risk and any contract addenda
- SRE/Platform owner - accepts operational risk and provides runbook
- CS - communicates to customer and maintains contact

Example email templates (Sales -> SE/Legal):
Subject: Waiver request: <Customer> - temporary cross-region routing until <YYYY-MM-DD>
Body:
Hi team,
We have a request from <Customer> to allow requests originating in <Region A> to be routed to <Region B> for the period <start> -> <end>. They claim <business justification>. Attached: waiver request form and data sensitivity attestation.
Please evaluate and fill out the risk summary and SRE acceptance checklist. We need an approval decision by <date>.
Thanks,
<AE Name>

Operator runbook (condensed):
- Step 0: Create a waiver folder in /waivers/<tenant-id>/ with request + approvals.
- Step 1: Create a feature-flagged routing rule in staging; run full synthetic suite.
- Step 2: If passing, schedule a low-traffic gradual rollout (5% -> 25% -> 100% over 2h, monitor).
- Step 3: Monitor waiver telemetry dashboard for 2x baseline window. If any alert fires, trigger immediate rollback and notify stakeholders.
- Step 4: Document the rollout window and confirm with customer.
- Step 5: At TTL-30d, re-evaluate with product privacy; if renewal required, repeat sign-off.

Rollback playbook (emergency):
- Trigger: sustained alert or Legal revocation.
- Action: run `waiver rollback --tenant <tenant-id>` to reinstate region pin.
- Verify: confirm 0% cross-region routing for 10m and no increase in 5xx errors.
- Postmortem: one business day update, 3-day root cause, 2-week blameless retro.

Acceptance criteria (final approval to go-live):
- Legal signs waiver (explicit TTL or permanent exception with contract amendment)
- Product Privacy confirms mitigations and telemetry coverage
- SRE completes staging + gradual rollout plan and validates rollback command
- CS confirms customer acknowledgement of residual risk and communications

Known open questions / TODOs:
- What counts as "regulated PII" for a waiver vs. mandatory denial? (Legal to enumerate canonical list).
- Auto-revocation policy for long-lived waivers (should we force re-review at 6-12 months?).
- Billing/chargeback: if waiver increases egress costs, who bears? (Finance to propose default).
- Should we offer an SLA offset or credit if the waiver causes measurable reliability degradation? (Product decision).

Appendix: quick decision matrix (example)
- Low sensitivity data + short TTL (<7d): expedited review (SE + SRE)
- Medium sensitivity or TTL 7-90d: Legal + Privacy sign-off required
- High sensitivity or TTL >90d: Legal + Exec review + contract amendment required

Notes to reviewers:
- This doc is intentionally pragmatic: we want a repeatable, auditable trail that prevents ad-hoc exceptions.
- Where possible, prefer short TTLs and technical mitigations (pseudonymization, ephemeral caches) over broad permanent waivers.
- Link to canonical policy: CONFLUENCE:regional-data-policy (placeholder).

Change log:
- 2024-11-08: initial draft by Aisha Patel
- 2024-12-02: added SRE telemetry checklist (Markus Chen)
- 2025-01-15: updated sign-off matrix and rollback automation notes (Ruth Alvarez)
